MECHANISM: A pro-rata spin-off delivers child-company shares to parent holders regardless of their standalone demand for the child. Mandate, size, tax, operational or concentration constraints can create early liquidity supply; a buyer may earn normalization if the selling pressure exceeds fundamental and trading risk.
WHO_PAYS: Hypothesized parent holders choosing or needing to dispose of newly distributed child shares; there is no claim that every recipient is forced to sell.
WHY_PERSIST: Irregular events, small/new listings, temporary when-issued symbols, operational complexity, mandate mismatch and limited capacity can make the opportunity unattractive to large capital. Public anticipation can also eliminate the effect.
CHEAP_DATA_NOW: Nasdaq Trader publishes free public Equity Corporate Actions Alerts for Nasdaq-listed spin-offs. The alerts can state parent/child, ratio, record date, payment/ex date, when-issued child symbol and first trade date, and the first regular-way trading date. A separate Nasdaq Daily List historical product exists but is subscription-based, so no free complete historical census is claimed. A previously qualified Yahoo v8 daily raw-close route provides a prospective child-price schema; it must succeed for the selected future child without provider substitution. The same route can be used for SPY as a benchmark only after the event claim is persisted.
FATAL_PROBLEM: The route supports a clean prospective case but not a complete free historical population. The causal payer remains probabilistic: distribution creates ownership, not compulsory sale. When-issued trading can partly pre-price the flow, and first-regular-way close may already reflect part of the disposal pressure.
